The best free screen recorders

A screen recorder for a quick walkthrough, a bug report or a lesson. These free tools record your screen; they differ in what they need you to install, where the video goes and how much they can do.

We make Screen Recorder, one of the tools on this page. Every fact about the other tools comes from their own pages, linked under each one, as they read on 2026-10-24. Prices and features change: check each site before you choose.

How we compared them

  • Free to use for screen recording
  • Webcam in a corner and microphone
  • Sound from the computer
  • Where the video is kept: your device or a cloud
  • Install or browser

1. Screen Recorder (ours)

Best for: A quick screen, webcam or screen + webcam recording in the browser, kept on your device.

Good

  • Nothing to install and no account
  • Screen with your webcam in a corner, countdown, pause and resume
  • Trim the ends, then WebM, MP4 or GIF; open it in Video Editor to edit
  • Says what your browser can record, including sound from the screen

Not so good

  • Sound from the screen only where the browser shares it (Chrome and Edge)
  • No scenes, streaming or drawing on the screen
  • No share links: you send the file yourself

Open Screen Recorder

2. OBS Studio

Best for: Long recordings and live streaming with scenes, many sources and full control.

Good

  • Records and streams
  • Scenes made of many sources: screens, windows, cameras, pictures
  • Open source

Not so good

  • Has to be installed and set up; more to learn than a one-button recorder

OBS Studio website · Sources: OBS Studio home page

3. ShareX

Best for: Windows users who want screenshots and screen recordings, including GIFs, in one tool.

Good

  • Screen recording to a video or a GIF
  • Screenshots with many capture modes
  • Open source

Not so good

  • Windows only
  • Many settings to find your way through

ShareX website · Sources: ShareX home page

4. Loom

Best for: Teams that want a share link to every recording and comments on it.

Good

  • A share link right after recording
  • Screen and camera together

Not so good

  • Needs an account, and the video is uploaded to Loom
  • The free plan has limits; more needs a paid plan

Loom website · Sources: Loom pricing

Which one to choose

Screen Recorder is our pick for a quick recording you keep: open the page, choose the screen, the webcam or both, record, trim and save, with nothing installed and nothing uploaded. It does not stream, has no scenes and makes no share links.

Choose OBS Studio for long recordings, many sources and streaming, ShareX on Windows for screenshots and GIFs in one tool, or Loom when your team wants a share link for every video and is happy to keep them in Loom's cloud.

Questions

Which free screen recorder records the computer's sound?

OBS Studio records desktop sound. In the browser, Screen Recorder gets the sound of a tab in Chrome and Edge, and of the whole screen on Windows and ChromeOS; Firefox and Safari share none.

Can I record my screen without installing anything?

Yes. Screen Recorder runs in a desktop browser. Phones and tablets do not let web pages record the screen, so use the phone's own recorder there.

Is my recording uploaded?

Not with Screen Recorder, OBS Studio or ShareX unless you choose to; Loom keeps your videos in its cloud so it can give you a link.
